children: NVIDIA (NVDA) reports earnings November 17. Analysts expect EPS of $2.48 and revenue of $109.17 billion, up from $1.30 and $57.01 billion a year earlier.
NVIDIA reportedly cut about half its preapproved Asian buyers and asked data-center and cloud partners to ensure at least 51% of services go to non-Chinese firms, amid U.S. scrutiny of chip access.
NVIDIA revenue grew 106% year over year. Analysts estimate $303 billion in annual revenue, with about 70% growth next year. Chip supply, especially advanced packaging, remains the key constraint.
Republicans plan tighter chip export controls that could affect NVIDIA (NVDA). CEO Jensen Huang previously met President Donald Trump to discuss limits on NVIDIA chip exports.
Investor George Noble warned that NVIDIA’s customer financing and startup investments may create an interdependent AI spending cycle, drawing parallels with Cisco’s late-1990s vendor financing.
NVIDIA partnered with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to create AI-compute financing platforms, aiming to mobilize over $500 billion in third-party capital over time.
NVIDIA’s five-year credit-default-swap spread and debt insurance cost hit record highs in recent months, though its spread remained well below Oracle’s record level.
NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) is increasing chip-tracking efforts in Southeast Asia to combat smuggling, according to Bloomberg News.
NVIDIA is exploring a plan with Apollo Global Management to convert over 130 Brightspeed telecom sites across up to 20 states into AI data centers. No deal, site count or timeline is confirmed.
Officials in Taiwan and Singapore reportedly raised concerns that Alice Huang may have obtained sensitive information on NVIDIA chips. Singapore denied sharing the information.
